title: I. Sadducees; Hymenaeus and Philetus — spiritual-only or succession-by-procreation readings
pass_a_gloss: or because they set the resurrection in succession which happens through the procreation of children, as Theodoret hands down touching them, and Augustine touching the disciples of Severus and Hermias (Heresy 89 to Quodvultdeus). Hymenaeus and Philetus said that the resurrection had already happened (2 Timothy 2:18), because they judged that no other than a spiritual one — which stands as from sins through regeneration — stands as promised, as Haymo and Lyra explain: touching the Sadducees it stands as established from the Gospel history and the Acts belonging toward the Apostles. I.
pass_b_english: I. Concerning the Sadducees it is established from the Gospel history and the Acts of the Apostles. Hymenaeus and Philetus said that the resurrection had already happened (2 Timothy 2:18), because they judged that no other than a spiritual one — which is from sins through regeneration — is promised, as Haymo and Lyra explain: or because they set the resurrection in succession which happens through the procreation of children, as Theodoret hands down concerning them, and Augustine concerning the disciples of Severus and Hermias (Heresy 89 to Quodvultdeus).
source_text: I. De Sadduceis constat ex historia Euangelica & Actis Apostolorum. Hymenaeus & Philetus dicebant resurrectionem jam esse factam 2.Tim. 2.18. quia existimabant, non aliam quam spiritualem, quae e peccatis per regenerationem est, promitti, ut Haymo & Lyranus explicant: vel quia resurrectionem in successione, quae per procreationem liberorum fit, constituebant, ut Theodoretus de illis tradit, deque Severi & Hermiae discipulis Augustinus haeres. 89. ad Quodvultdeum.
